about: Every known way to cut what an AI coding agent costs: the parameters each one changes, and its potential on a workload you set. Each estimate is labelled by how much to trust it. Inspired by battleships.dev.

evidence.priced: arithmetic on published list prices; still a ceiling until measured on your tasks
evidence.measured: opthub ran it on real sessions; small n, said where it is
evidence.published: a vendor or practitioner figure for generic workloads, not measured here
evidence.guess: a stated range with a stated basis and no measurement behind it

scenarios.name: Prompt caching
scenarios.what: Mark the stable prefix (system prompt, tools, early turns) cacheable so repeat reads bill at 10% of the input price.

params.value: {"type":"ephemeral"} on the last stable block, or top-level auto-caching
tools → system → messages; nothing dynamic above the breakpoint

scenarios.opthub: detector · this workload already hits 96.8% (E1-F4), so nothing is left to win
scenarios.caveat: Worth up to 90% of input cost on a client that does not cache; worth nothing on one that already does.

scenarios.name: Cache TTL: 1 hour instead of 5 minutes
scenarios.what: Keep the cached prefix alive across pauses longer than five minutes, at twice the write price instead of 1.25×.
scenarios.opthub: measured · the sign flipped twice in an hour; two populations want opposite settings (E1b-F3)
scenarios.caveat: Pays only when gaps between turns are mostly 5–60 minutes. Decide per population by the write:read ratio in dollars, never globally.

scenarios.name: Exact-match response cache
scenarios.what: Answer a byte-identical request from the proxy's cache instead of calling the model.
scenarios.opthub: catalog arm litellm-response-cache · not yet run
scenarios.caveat: Agent turns almost never repeat byte for byte. It pays for retries, re-runs and repeated CI jobs.

scenarios.name: Semantic cache
scenarios.what: Answer a near-duplicate prompt from a vector store of earlier answers.

params.value: redis or pgvector, an embedding model

scenarios.opthub: catalog · runnable:false, needs a gateway in the request path
scenarios.caveat: Published 30–50% is for support and FAQ traffic. Coding sessions rarely repeat a question; a near match with different files underneath is a wrong answer.

scenarios.name: Cache pre-warming
scenarios.what: Send a max_tokens 0 request ahead of the first real turn so the prefix is cached when the user arrives.

params.value: 0 on a warm-up request with the same prefix

scenarios.caveat: A latency lever: it pays one cache write early and saves nothing on cost.

scenarios.name: Move to the newer, cheaper model version
scenarios.what: Claude Opus 5.5 lists at $4/$20 per million tokens against Opus 5's $5/$25, with the same context and tokenizer.

params.value: set explicitly: its default is medium, one level below Opus 5
omit or {type: adaptive}; it cannot be disabled

scenarios.opthub: priced · this machine already runs 10 of 65 sessions on Opus 5.5
scenarios.caveat: Breaking changes to handle: forced tool_choice returns 400, thinking cannot be disabled. Re-check quality on your own tasks.

scenarios.name: Route whole tasks to a mid model
scenarios.what: Send every request of a task that a mid model can handle to Sonnet instead of Opus.
scenarios.opthub: measured · 2 sandbox re-runs: Sonnet took 2× the turns and cost 2.4–3.9× more; one scored 27 points worse (J3)
scenarios.caveat: The per-token price falls 60%. The per-task price can rise, because a weaker model takes more turns. Only a re-run tells you which.

scenarios.name: Route subagents and background calls
scenarios.what: Keep the coding loop on the frontier model; send Task subagents and Claude Code's small calls (titles, summaries) to cheaper models.
scenarios.opthub: LLM Light profile laptop-guarded · catalog arm litellm-route-side-calls · routing verified on mock upstreams
scenarios.caveat: Without a route, an Opus baseline pays Opus prices for session titles. A subagent doing real reasoning may do it worse on Sonnet.

scenarios.name: Cascade: try small, escalate on failure
scenarios.what: Answer with the cheap model first and re-ask the frontier model only when a check fails.
scenarios.caveat: Every escalation pays twice. It saves only when the check is cheap and the small model passes it most of the time.

scenarios.name: Offload to an open-weights model
scenarios.what: Serve part of the work from a local or serverless open-weights model (Qwen3-Coder, Llama) behind the same API.
scenarios.opthub: measured n=1 · 7.1× cheaper and 18 points worse on the blind score
scenarios.caveat: Cheap is easy; doing the same job is the question. Needs a quality gate on every routed class.

scenarios.name: Advisor pattern
scenarios.what: A mid model executes; the frontier model is consulted as a tool only on the hard steps.

params.value: advisor model claude-opus-5; must be at least as capable as the executor

scenarios.caveat: Advisor calls are billed at the frontier rate. The win depends on how few steps need it.

scenarios.name: Plan on the frontier, execute on mid
scenarios.what: One frontier call writes the plan; a mid model carries it out step by step.
scenarios.caveat: A bad plan is executed faithfully and cheaply. Overlaps the advisor pattern; do not count both.

scenarios.name: Distil or fine-tune a small model
scenarios.what: Train a small model on the frontier model's answers for one narrow, high-volume task.

params.value: frontier outputs on your task, labelled

scenarios.opthub: recommended for LLM Light's classifier (distil Jev) in docs/demo-thesis.md
scenarios.caveat: Weeks of work and a training bill. Only for one narrow task at volume.

scenarios.name: Lower the effort level
scenarios.what: Ask for less thinking and fewer, more consolidated tool calls on routine work.
scenarios.opthub: catalog arms effort-medium, effort-low · E3 will measure
scenarios.caveat: Routine work often holds at medium. Hard reasoning gets shallower exactly where it was needed.

scenarios.name: Cap thinking tokens
scenarios.what: Put a ceiling on how many tokens the model may think per turn.
scenarios.opthub: catalog arm claude-thinking-cap · LLM Light sandbox-lean, ci-strict
scenarios.caveat: Thinking is billed as output. Overlaps the effort lever; do not count both.

scenarios.name: Shorter output
scenarios.what: Ask for terse answers, structured output, diffs instead of whole files.
scenarios.caveat: A cap that truncates mid-answer forces a retry, which costs more than it saved.

scenarios.name: Task budget
scenarios.what: Give the agent a token budget for the whole task so it paces itself and finishes instead of running long.
scenarios.caveat: Bounds the long tail of runaway tasks; average tasks are unaffected.

scenarios.name: Split sessions between tasks
scenarios.what: Start a fresh session, or clear it, when the work moves to an unrelated task, so later turns stop re-sending dead history.
scenarios.opthub: top-ranked lever (E1-F5: 52.9% of spend is sessions with median context ≥250k) · J3 marks separable sessions; the largest held 16 tasks
scenarios.caveat: Needs the person or a classifier to notice the topic changed. Saving counted at 25–50% of the history cost of separable sessions.

scenarios.name: Compaction
scenarios.what: Summarise earlier turns when the context grows past a threshold.
scenarios.opthub: catalog arm context-compaction
scenarios.caveat: Each compaction pays for a summary and a fresh cache write. A summary can drop the detail a later turn needed.

scenarios.name: Clear old tool results
scenarios.what: Drop old tool results or thinking blocks from the history before each request.
scenarios.caveat: A context-window tool, not a saving: each clear rewrites the cached history. In Anthropic's own measured run it cost more than it saved.

scenarios.name: Drop unused tools and MCP servers
scenarios.what: Send only the tool definitions a task can use. Every tool schema is re-sent on every turn.

params.value: load only the MCP servers named for this run

scenarios.opthub: savings.py lever A (prefix-trim) · E2 will measure
scenarios.caveat: Removing a tool the task turns out to need costs a failed turn.

scenarios.name: Load tools on demand
scenarios.what: Mark most tools deferred and give the model a search tool; definitions load only when found.
scenarios.caveat: Pays with many MCP tools. Overlaps dropping unused tools; do not count both.

scenarios.name: Retrieve instead of stuffing
scenarios.what: Fetch the relevant files or passages per turn instead of keeping whole documents in context.

params.value: search / embeddings over the repo or docs

scenarios.caveat: Workload dependent. Coding agents already read files on demand.

scenarios.name: Prompt compression
scenarios.what: Compress prompts with a model or heuristic before they are sent.
scenarios.opthub: headroom is installed in the sandbox template · not measured
scenarios.caveat: Changing the prefix breaks the prompt cache. On a cache-heavy workload it can cost more than it saves.

scenarios.name: Stop re-reading the same files
scenarios.what: Avoid reading the same file into context again when it has not changed.

params.value: prefer targeted reads (offset/limit) and grep over full re-reads

scenarios.caveat: Hard to enforce from outside the agent.

scenarios.name: Batch API for work that can wait
scenarios.what: Send requests nobody is waiting on through the Message Batches API at half price.
scenarios.opthub: J3 · best case 50% of deferrable spend; worst case negative when the cache is lost
scenarios.caveat: Batch requests are single-shot: no tool loop inside a batch, and cache hits are best-effort. On a cache-heavy agent it can cost more.

scenarios.name: Fewer round trips
scenarios.what: Do more per turn: parallel tool calls, or let code call tools in a loop without a model turn each time.

params.value: on (default); return all results in one message

scenarios.caveat: Every saved turn saves one full re-send of the context. Needs tools designed for it.

scenarios.name: Stop paying for failed requests
scenarios.what: Cut retries, timeouts and requests aborted after tokens were billed.

params.value: for long outputs, so a timeout does not discard a paid answer

scenarios.caveat: Needs the retry rate measured first.

scenarios.name: Count tokens before sending
scenarios.what: Reject or trim a request that would be unusually large before it is billed.
scenarios.caveat: Adds a call. Useful only as a guard against outliers.

scenarios.name: Fast mode
scenarios.what: The same model at up to 2.5× output speed, at twice the price. A spend, for urgent interactive work.
scenarios.opthub: J3 flags blocking-now + interactive sessions as where paying more is justified
scenarios.caveat: Shown as spend. Never net it against savings.

scenarios.name: Cap agent turns and stop loops
scenarios.what: Stop an agent that loops instead of letting its context, and cost, grow.
scenarios.opthub: measured · loops were 1.4% of spend on one developer's month (E1-F2)
scenarios.caveat: Bounds the tail. An unfinished task is scored as unfinished.

scenarios.name: Budgets and rate limits
scenarios.what: Hard spend ceilings per run, key, team or day.
scenarios.opthub: catalog arm litellm-proxy-budget · triage re-run batch cap
scenarios.caveat: A guard: it bounds the worst case and saves nothing on a normal day. --max-budget-usd stops only after it is crossed.

scenarios.name: Cost attribution and showback
scenarios.what: Tag every request with team and project and show each team its spend.
scenarios.opthub: Hub → Sessions and Triage do this per session today
scenarios.caveat: Indirect: people change behaviour when they see the bill.

scenarios.name: Choose where the model is served
scenarios.what: The same model is billed differently on the Claude API, Bedrock, Vertex AI and Foundry.

params.value: Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry

scenarios.opthub: the sandbox runs on Bedrock, laptops on the Claude API
scenarios.caveat: Partner pricing differs by contract and region; features differ by platform (fast mode is Claude API only).

scenarios.name: Shut down idle sandboxes
scenarios.what: Pause or stop an agent sandbox while the agent waits on a model call or a person.
scenarios.opthub: E2B arms run with a 30-minute sandbox timeout
scenarios.caveat: A cold start costs seconds per resume. Compare providers' per-second pricing at battleships.dev.

scenarios.name: Right-size sandbox machines
scenarios.what: Give each sandbox the vCPU and RAM its workload uses, not the template default.
scenarios.opthub: sandbox/e2b/harness/e2b.Dockerfile is a bigger box for sidecars
scenarios.caveat: An undersized box turns a CPU wait into a longer, costlier model session.

scenarios.name: Quantise self-hosted models
scenarios.what: Serve open-weights models at lower precision to fit cheaper hardware.
scenarios.opthub: sandbox/e2b/openmodel serves Ollama
scenarios.caveat: Only for self-hosted spend. Lower precision can cost quality on hard tasks.

scenarios.name: Serving efficiency (self-hosted)
scenarios.what: Continuous batching, prefix caching and speculative decoding on your own GPUs.

params.value: continuous batching, enable prefix caching, speculative decoding

scenarios.caveat: Only for self-hosted spend. Throughput gains need steady traffic.
